sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: There are so many small delights that people have found themselves longing for during this past year.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，人们发现自己渴望着许多微小的快乐。

sentences.en: The sudden hush in a movie theater as the lights go down.
sentences.zh: 电影院里灯光暗下时那突如其来的寂静。

sentences.en: The roar of an airplane's engines as it accelerates down a runway bound for a new destination.
sentences.zh: 飞机引擎在跑道上加速、准备飞往新目的地时的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: The happy buzz of conversation and laughter in a crowded restaurant.
sentences.zh: 在拥挤的餐厅里，欢快的交谈声和笑声。

sentences.en: Another tiny pleasure that has become more rare during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 另一个在疫情期间变得更为罕见的微小乐趣。

sentences.en: The unexpected moments that we call coincidences.
sentences.zh: 那些我们称之为巧合的意料之外的时刻。

sentences.en: Staying at home has meant fewer opportunities for chance encounters,
sentences.zh: 待在家里意味着偶遇的机会减少了，

sentences.en: like running into a neighbor on a vacation,
sentences.zh: 比如在度假时偶遇邻居，

sentences.en: or discovering during a chat at the water cooler that you share the same birthday as a co-worker.
sentences.zh: 或者在茶水间聊天时发现自己和同事同年同月同日生。

sentences.en: As the pandemic is brought under control in some parts of the world,
sentences.zh: 随着疫情在世界某些地区得到控制，

sentences.en: and people start to move about, we are more likely to experience coincidences.
sentences.zh: 人们开始四处走动，我们更有可能经历巧合。

sentences.en: And that made us think about an episode a couple of years ago when two different listeners called into Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这让我们想起了几年前的一集节目，当时有两个不同的听众打进“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I was a student at the University of Rhode Island, and we were in this writing class.
sentences.zh: 我当时是罗德岛大学的学生，我们在上这门写作课。

sentences.en: This is Amanda Birch.
sentences.zh: 这是阿曼达·伯奇。

sentences.en: She told us she was chatting with the teacher of her writing class.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我们，她正在和她的写作课老师聊天。

sentences.en: The teacher mentioned that she lived in a small town in Vermont.
sentences.zh: 老师提到她住在佛蒙特州的一个小镇上。

sentences.en: The same small town, it turned out, where Amanda's mother had grown up.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，那是阿曼达的母亲长大的同一个小镇。

sentences.en: The teacher asked Amanda what her mother's maiden name was.
sentences.zh: 老师问阿曼达她母亲的婚前姓氏是什么。

sentences.en: Amanda told her.
sentences.zh: 阿曼达告诉了她。

sentences.en: She just kind of drops her pen and she goes,
sentences.zh: 她只是把笔一扔，然后说道：

sentences.en: You're not going to believe this, but I live in the house where your mother grew up.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不会相信，但我住的房子就是你母亲长大的房子。

sentences.en: The other listener who called us was Sarah Toporov.
sentences.zh: 另一位给我们打电话的听众是萨拉·托波罗夫。

sentences.en: She called us on a scratchy phone line from Paris.
sentences.zh: 她通过一条杂音很重的电话线从巴黎打来电话。

sentences.en: Sarah's an American, but was living in France.
sentences.zh: 萨拉是个美国人，但当时住在法国。

sentences.en: One time, she was at a house party, and someone there told her there was another American in the room.
sentences.zh: 有一次，她在参加一个家庭派对，那里有人告诉她房间里还有另一个美国人。

sentences.en: So she went over to say hello.
sentences.zh: 于是她走过去打招呼。

sentences.en: They started talking, and...
sentences.zh: 他们开始交谈，然后……

sentences.en: So it turns out that this house party in Paris grew up in the exact same house in Poughkeepsie, New York, as my father.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，这个在巴黎参加派对的人，长大的房子和我父亲在纽约州波基普西的房子一模一样。

sentences.en: What are the odds?
sentences.zh: 几率有多大？

sentences.en: Just by chance, two listeners on different continents calling in with such similar stories.
sentences.zh: 纯属巧合，身处不同大洲的两位听众打进电话，讲述着如此相似的故事。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we explore the mathematics of coincidences.
sentences.zh: 本周的“隐藏的大脑”，我们来探讨巧合背后的数学原理。

sentences.en: That particular kind of coincidence, meeting an acquaintance or somebody you're familiar with,
sentences.zh: 那种特定类型的巧合，在一个非常奇怪的地方遇到一个熟人或你熟悉的人，

sentences.en: in a very strange place, perhaps 80% of all the coincidences I've heard fall into that category.
sentences.zh: 我听过的所有巧合中，大约80%都属于这一类。

sentences.en: And we ask why these little moments feel so psychologically significant.
sentences.zh: 我们不禁要问，为什么这些微小的时刻在心理上感觉如此具有重大意义。

sentences.en: Whenever you see something that you can't explain, the natural human instinct is to try to understand it.
sentences.zh: 每当你看到无法解释的事情时，人类的本能反应就是试图去理解它。

sentences.en: But that can also mean that sometimes we over-explain things.
sentences.zh: 但这有时也意味着我们会过度解释事物。

sentences.en: We're starting today with a story about Whisper.
sentences.zh: 我们今天从一个关于“耳语”的故事开始。

sentences.en: And just so you can understand this coincidence story,
sentences.zh: 为了让你们理解这个巧合的故事，

sentences.en: we're going to first explain what Whisper is and how it works.
sentences.zh: 我们将首先解释什么是“耳语”以及它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Whisper is an app that allows users to connect anonymously online.
sentences.zh: “耳语”是一个允许用户在网上匿名交流的应用程序。

sentences.en: They can post messages or secrets.
sentences.zh: 他们可以发布消息或秘密。

sentences.en: These are called whispers.
sentences.zh: 这些被称为“耳语”。

sentences.en: And strangers can respond with their own whispers.
sentences.zh: 陌生人可以用他们自己的“耳语”来回应。

sentences.en: We've asked a few producers to read out some of these whispers.
sentences.zh: 我们请了几位制作人朗读其中一些“耳语”。

sentences.en: The messages are short, about the length of a tweet, and they range from the silly...
sentences.zh: 这些信息很短，大约有一条推文的长度，内容从傻气的……

sentences.en: As a teacher, I'm not supposed to have favorite students, but I definitely do.
sentences.zh: 作为一名老师，我不应该有最喜欢的学生，但我确实有。

sentences.en: I just want someone to...
sentences.zh: 我只是想要某人……

sentences.en: ...to the very serious.
sentences.zh: ……到非常严肃的。

sentences.en: I'm having an abortion on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我周一要做流产手术。

sentences.en: My husband cheated on me.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫对我背叛了。

sentences.en: Should I forgive him?
sentences.zh: 我应该原谅他吗？

sentences.en: Some months ago, the folks at Whisper got in touch to tell us a story about an interesting coincidence that happened on their site.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，“耳语”的工作人员联系我们，给我们讲了一个发生在他们网站上的有趣巧合的故事。

sentences.en: Lauren Hudson is 27, and she turned to Whisper at one of the darkest moments of her life.
sentences.zh: 劳伦·哈德逊27岁，在她一生中最黑暗的时刻之一，她求助于“耳语”。

sentences.en: I was in a really bad relationship.
sentences.zh: 我当时处在一段非常糟糕的恋爱关系中。

sentences.en: There was a lot of domestic violence involved.
sentences.zh: 其中涉及大量的家庭暴力。

sentences.en: And I didn't really know what to do or how to reach out to people or how to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道该怎么办，或者如何向人们倾诉，或者如何谈论它。

sentences.en: So I used the app to connect with other women and to kind of vent and find empowerment to get away from the person that I was with.
sentences.zh: 所以我用这个应用程序与其他女性交流，发泄一下，并找到摆脱我身边这个人的力量。

sentences.en: Lauren was having trouble opening up about what was happening with her friends and family.
sentences.zh: 劳伦很难向朋友和家人敞开心扉谈论所发生的事情。

sentences.en: I think I was scared, to be completely honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我想我是害怕的。

sentences.en: I think I had a lot of fear.
sentences.zh: 我想我有很多恐惧。

sentences.en: And I didn't want, like, any police involved.
sentences.zh: 而且我不想牵涉到什么警察之类的。

sentences.en: I didn't want, like...
sentences.zh: 我不想像……

sentences.en: I didn't want it to turn into, like, this whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我不想让它变成这样一整桩事情。

sentences.en: But on Whisper, she could be anonymous.
sentences.zh: 但在“耳语”上，她可以匿名。

sentences.en: She could seek support without all the immediate consequences.
sentences.zh: 她可以在没有所有直接后果的情况下寻求支持。

sentences.en: It was there, in one of these threads, that she started talking to a man.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，在其中一个帖子下，她开始和一个男人交谈。

sentences.en: Lauren was touched by how much compassion he seemed to have for her, a complete stranger.
sentences.zh: 劳伦被他对她这个完全陌生的人所表现出的同情心深深打动了。

sentences.en: It was almost as if he genuinely wanted to know how I was.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像他是真心想知道我过得怎么样。

sentences.en: Even though he didn't know who I was, and he knew that it was anonymous, and who knows who he's talking to,
sentences.zh: 尽管他不知道我是谁，而且他知道那是匿名的，谁知道他在和谁说话，

sentences.en: he just genuinely wanted to know if I was okay.
sentences.zh: 他只是真心想知道我是否还好。

sentences.en: He was in a town nearby, another coincidence perhaps, and they started exchanging messages.
sentences.zh: 他在附近的一个镇上，也许又是另一个巧合，他们开始互发信息。

sentences.en: They connected immediately, decided to meet in person.
sentences.zh: 他们一拍即合，决定亲自见面。

sentences.en: We got together, and we went to Applebee's, and we sat and we talked for, like...
sentences.zh: 我们聚在一起，去了苹果蜂餐厅，坐下来聊了大约……

sentences.en: I think it was, like, almost two hours that we just sat and talked.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有将近两个小时，我们只是坐着聊天。

sentences.en: They became more and more inseparable.
sentences.zh: 他们的关系变得越来越密不可分。

sentences.en: Lauren ended her unhealthy relationship and started dating this guy from Whisper, Eric.
sentences.zh: 劳伦结束了她那段不健康的恋爱关系，开始和这个来自“耳语”的家伙埃里克约会。

sentences.en: And everything was going great.
sentences.zh: 一切都进展顺利。

sentences.en: But Lauren was a little nervous about meeting Eric's family.
sentences.zh: 但劳伦对去见埃里克的家人有点紧张。

sentences.en: Eric had brought Lauren home to have dinner with them,
sentences.zh: 埃里克带劳伦回家和他们一起吃晚饭，

sentences.en: and the whole time she was anxious.
sentences.zh: 她一整都感到焦虑。

sentences.en: Like, my palms were sweating, and I felt, like, really hot, you know, so...
sentences.zh: 比如，我的手心在出汗，我觉得浑身发热，你知道的，所以……

sentences.en: I didn't know if, like, if it was going down well or if I was totally blowing it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这到底进展顺利还是我彻底搞砸了。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: She was especially nervous about Eric's sister, Amanda.
sentences.zh: 她对埃里克的姐姐阿曼达尤其感到紧张。

sentences.en: You know, I knew when I first met her there, the first couple times that we hung out and stuff,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当我在那里第一次见到她时，前几次我们一起出去玩的时候，

sentences.en: I knew that there was a little bit of a distance there,
sentences.zh: 我知道之间有点距离感，

sentences.en: and I knew that every time I went over to, you know, hang out with Eric and his family,
sentences.zh: 我也知道每次我去和埃里克以及他的家人一起玩时，

sentences.en: that those walls would slowly break down.
sentences.zh: 那些隔阂会慢慢打破。

sentences.en: But Lauren was impatient.
sentences.zh: 但劳伦有些不耐烦。

sentences.en: She and Eric were getting engaged.
sentences.zh: 她和埃里克快要订婚了。

sentences.en: Lauren understood Amanda's attitude.
sentences.zh: 劳伦理解阿曼达的态度。

sentences.en: She felt the same toward the girls her younger brother would bring home.
sentences.zh: 她对她弟弟带回家的女孩也有同感。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll see them next week, you know, or maybe I'll never see them again.
sentences.zh: 也许我下周会见到她们，你知道的，或者也许我再也见不到她们了。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: So that was kind of, like, what I had in my head.
sentences.zh: 所以这差不多就是我脑子里想的。

sentences.en: I was like, well, I hope that, you know, I'm thinking,
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我希望，你知道的，我在想，

sentences.en: I hope that they know that I'm not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们知道我哪儿也不去。

sentences.en: Lauren wasn't going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 劳伦哪儿也不去。

sentences.en: She and Eric were getting engaged.
sentences.zh: 她和埃里克快要订婚了。

sentences.en: Eric, in fact, had a flair for the romantic, bringing her roses,
sentences.zh: 事实上，埃里克很有浪漫情调，给她送玫瑰，

sentences.en: comforting her with her favorite movie after a tough day.
sentences.zh: 在艰难的一天后用她最喜欢的电影安慰她。

sentences.en: And he would tell his family about all this.
sentences.zh: 他会把这一切告诉他的家人。

sentences.en: So why couldn't Lauren break through with Amanda?
sentences.zh: 那为什么劳伦无法打破与阿曼达的僵局呢？

sentences.en: All this time, Lauren was still on Whisper.
sentences.zh: 这段时间，劳伦仍然在使用“耳语”。

sentences.en: Now I use it, instead of me looking for help, I use it to help others.
sentences.zh: 现在我用它不是为了寻求帮助，而是用它来帮助别人。

sentences.en: That's my way of giving back,
sentences.zh: 这是我回馈社会的方式，

sentences.en: because the Whisper community helped me when I needed them.
sentences.zh: 因为当我需要的时候，“耳语”社区曾帮助过我。

sentences.en: One day, she started exchanging messages with a woman
sentences.zh: 有一天，她开始和一个正在经历非常痛苦的分手的女人互发信息。

sentences.en: who was going through a very painful breakup.
sentences.zh: 我发了一条长信息，基本上是说没关系，

sentences.en: I sent a big message, basically saying that it's okay,
sentences.zh: 每个人都会经历心碎，

sentences.en: everyone goes through heartaches,
sentences.zh: 外面还会有很多其他人。

sentences.en: and there will be many more people out there.
sentences.zh: 作为一种鼓励的方式，

sentences.en: As a way to offer encouragement,
sentences.zh: 劳伦向这个女人讲述了她自己幸福的恋爱关系。

sentences.en: Lauren told a woman about her own happy relationship.
sentences.zh: 这个女人问劳伦她的未婚夫为她做过的最贴心的事情是什么。

sentences.en: The woman asked Lauren about the nicest thing her fiancé had done for her.
sentences.zh: 劳伦向她讲述了埃里克用她最喜欢的电影给她惊喜的那一天。

sentences.en: Lauren told her about the day Eric surprised her with her favorite movie.
sentences.zh: 在我生日那天，我在工作很不顺心。

sentences.en: On my birthday, I had a really bad day at work.
sentences.zh: 那就像那种日子，你知道的，

sentences.en: It was like one of those days where, like, you know,
sentences.zh: 你醒来，从你双脚着地的那一刻起，

sentences.en: you wake up and just from the moment you put your feet on the floor,
sentences.zh: 就像，所有事情都不对劲。

sentences.en: like, everything goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是，我那天不想见他。

sentences.en: So I was just, I didn't want to see him that day.
sentences.zh: 我当时糟透了。

sentences.en: I was just miserable.
sentences.zh: 我只想回家。

sentences.en: I just wanted to be home.
sentences.zh: 就像，我只是觉得，我只想去睡觉。

sentences.en: Like, I was just, like, I just want to go to bed.
sentences.zh: 而他用这些美丽的花、这些玫瑰给了我一个惊喜，

sentences.en: And he surprised me with these beautiful flowers, these roses,
sentences.zh: 他还带着《恋恋笔记本》，

sentences.en: and he had the notebook,
sentences.zh: 那是我有生以来最喜欢的感人爱情故事。

sentences.en: which is my favorite, like, sappy love story of all time.
sentences.zh: 劳伦讲完她的故事，等待着回复。

sentences.en: Lauren finished telling her story and waited for a reply.
sentences.zh: 在我把那个故事发给她之后，她的第一反应是，

sentences.en: Her first response after I sent that story to her,
sentences.zh: 她说，劳伦？

sentences.en: she's like, Lauren?
sentences.zh: 劳伦？

sentences.en: Lauren?
sentences.zh: 劳伦，我当时想，你怎么知道我的名字？

sentences.en: Lauren, I was like, how do you know my name?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为这一切都是匿名的。

sentences.en: You know, because it's all anonymous.
sentences.zh: 她说，我是阿曼达。

sentences.en: And she's like, this is Amanda.
sentences.zh: 阿曼达，埃里克的姐姐，

sentences.en: Amanda, Eric's sister,
sentences.zh: 正是她一直在现实生活中拼命想要建立联系的那个人。

sentences.en: the very person she'd been trying so desperately to connect with in real life.
sentences.zh: 劳伦说这个巧合改变了她与阿曼达的整个关系。

sentences.en: Lauren says this coincidence changed her whole relationship with Amanda.
sentences.zh: 在网上随机连接并透露彼此的私密细节，

sentences.en: Connecting randomly online and revealing intimate details about themselves
sentences.zh: 让两个女人感觉更亲近了。

sentences.en: made the two women feel closer.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都经历过这种巧合。

sentences.en: Many of us have experienced these kinds of coincidences.
sentences.zh: 你在上大学的第一天撞见了幼儿园的朋友，

sentences.en: You bump into your kindergarten friend your first day in college,
sentences.zh: 或者你在派对上遇到某人，发现她住在你爸爸在波基普西的童年老家里。

sentences.en: or you meet someone at a party and discover she lives in your dad's childhood home in Poughkeepsie.
sentences.zh: 当这些巧合发生在我们的生活中时，它们感觉就像魔法一样。

sentences.en: When these kinds of coincidences happen in our lives, they feel like magic.
sentences.zh: 但正如任何数学家都会告诉你的那样，

sentences.en: But as any mathematician will tell you,
sentences.zh: 那些感觉不同寻常甚至不可能的事情实际上相当普遍。

sentences.en: things that feel unusual or even impossible are actually fairly common.
sentences.zh: 数学家约瑟夫·马祖尔深知这一点，

sentences.en: Mathematician Joseph Mazur knows this,
sentences.zh: 但他很不情愿写一本会打破这种魔法的书。

sentences.en: but he was reluctant to write a book that would dispel the magic.
sentences.zh: 巧合是美妙的故事。

sentences.en: Coincidences are wonderful stories.
sentences.zh: 巧合是美妙的故事。

sentences.en: I don't want to blow the stories in favor of the mathematics because,
sentences.zh: 我不想为了数学而破坏故事，因为，

sentences.en: you know, I was hitting a nerve on coincidences.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在巧合这个话题上触动了一根神经。

sentences.en: In the end, though, Joseph did write his book.
sentences.zh: 不过，约瑟夫最终还是写了他的书。

sentences.en: It's called Fluke, The Math and Myth of Coincidence.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《奇迹：巧合的数学与神话》。

sentences.en: It's full of stories of people who find themselves experiencing things that feel so unlikely.
sentences.zh: 里面充满了各种人们经历奇妙巧合的故事，那些感觉极不可能发生的事情。

sentences.en: But Joseph Mazur says if you study this for a while,
sentences.zh: 但约瑟夫·马祖尔说，如果你研究一段时间，

sentences.en: the coincidences start to fall into certain categories.
sentences.zh: 这些巧合就会开始归入某些特定的类别。

sentences.en: And the stories we heard from our two listeners,

sentences.zh: 像机器人一样移动、非常可预测的事物，

sentences.en: that is just a mindless machine.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个没有思想的机器。

sentences.en: But when your Roomba is going around randomly,
sentences.zh: 但当你的Roomba到处随机乱走时，

sentences.en: well, now it wants to go over there a little bit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在它想去那边一点。

sentences.en: Now it wants to move over here.
sentences.zh: 现在它想移到这边来。

sentences.en: Now it realizes it didn't clean that side of the pool over there.
sentences.zh: 现在它意识到刚才没有清理泳池的那个边。

sentences.en: Things that behave randomly start to get a little sense of a mind.
sentences.zh: 行为随机的事物开始表现出一点点心思。

sentences.en: Now, people aren't crazy.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们并没有疯。

sentences.en: You don't think it's like your mother, right?
sentences.zh: 你不会觉得它就像你的母亲，对吧？

sentences.en: Or your spouse who's vacuuming the living room.
sentences.zh: 或者像在吸尘客厅的配偶。

sentences.en: But it starts to look just a little bit more mindful.
sentences.zh: 但它开始显得稍微更有思想一点了。

sentences.en: In fact, a Roomba is a good example.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Roomba就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: People actually do name their Roombas.
sentences.zh: 人们真的会给他们的Roomba起名字。

sentences.en: You can buy outfits to dress it up.
sentences.zh: 你可以买衣服来为它打扮。

sentences.en: If you Google this online,
sentences.zh: 如果你在网上搜一下，

sentences.en: you'll find all kinds of examples of people thinking of their Roomba
sentences.zh: 你会发现各种各样的例子，人们认为他们的Roomba

sentences.en: as having perhaps a little bit more of a mind than it really does.
sentences.zh: 似乎比实际上更有那么一点点思想。

sentences.en: I want to talk to you a little bit about the subject of coincidences.
sentences.zh: 我想跟你聊聊巧合这个主题。

sentences.en: And I thought of you and your work because it feels to me that when something unusual happens to us
sentences.zh: 我想到了你和你的研究，因为我觉得当一些不寻常的事情发生在我们身上时，

sentences.en: and we stop and we say,
sentences.zh: 我们会停下来然后说：

sentences.en: that is weird.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I was just reading this word in a book a second ago
sentences.zh: 我刚才在书里读到这个词，

sentences.en: and someone in the room around me mentions the very same word.
sentences.zh: 然后我周围房间里就有人提到了同一个词。

sentences.en: And it makes you stop and look up just like I stop and look at that underwater Roomba.
sentences.zh: 这让你停下来抬头看，就像我停下来看着那个水下Roomba一样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: That's a case where something unusual happens.
sentences.zh: 这是一个发生不寻常事情的例子。

sentences.en: It was unpredictable and you try to explain it.
sentences.zh: 它是不可预测的，而你试图去解释它。

sentences.en: You can explain these kinds of random coincidences in lots of different ways.
sentences.zh: 你可以用很多不同的方式来解释这种随机的巧合。

sentences.en: There are lots of different kinds of causal structures we might be able to put on it.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会在它上面附加许多不同种类的因果结构。

sentences.en: But some of them involve giving it more meaning than it actually has.
sentences.zh: 但其中一些涉及赋予它比实际更多的意义。

sentences.en: This is what underwater Roombas have to do with coincidences.
sentences.zh: 这就是水下Roomba与巧合的关系。

sentences.en: Like a robot that does something unexpected,
sentences.zh: 就像做出意想不到举动的机器人一样，

sentences.en: coincidences cry out for meaning or explanation because they're out of the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 巧合呼唤着意义或解释，因为它们异乎寻常。

sentences.en: We start to seek patterns even when there aren't any.
sentences.zh: 即使在没有任何规律的情况下，我们也开始寻找规律。

sentences.en: My favorite example of this in the world of psychology
sentences.zh: 在心理学领域，我最喜欢的关于这个的例子，

sentences.en: is actually a phenomenon first documented by my PhD advisor, Tom Gilovich,
sentences.zh: 其实是一个最早由我的博士导师汤姆·吉洛维奇（Tom Gilovich）

sentences.en: and the brilliant psychologist Amos Tversky
sentences.zh: 和杰出的心理学家阿莫斯·特沃斯基（Amos Tversky）记录的现象，

sentences.en: is the illusion of the hot hand in basketball.
sentences.zh: 即篮球运动中的“热手错觉”。

sentences.en: Danny Green again from downtown.
sentences.zh: 丹尼·格林再次从三分线外出手。

sentences.en: He's hit six in a row going back to game two.
sentences.zh: 算上第二场比赛，他已经连续投中六个了。

sentences.en: The myth is that when shooting free throws, basketball players get on a roll.
sentences.zh: 这种迷思是，当罚球时，篮球运动员会处于手感火热的状态。

sentences.en: People believe that basketball players get a hot hand
sentences.zh: 人们相信篮球运动员会手感火热，

sentences.en: and that there are times when they're on
sentences.zh: 并且在某些时候他们状态极佳，

sentences.en: and the chance of making a basket is higher after they've just made one
sentences.zh: 在刚刚投中一个球之后，再次投中的几率

sentences.en: than after they've just missed one.
sentences.zh: 要高于刚刚投失一个球之后。

sentences.en: Epley isn't saying basketball players don't have streaks.
sentences.zh: 埃普利并不是说篮球运动员没有连续投中的状态。

sentences.en: He's saying we draw the wrong conclusion about these streaks.
sentences.zh: 他是说我们对这些连中状态得出了错误的结论。

sentences.en: Let's imagine that they're a good shooter and they shoot 50% from the field.
sentences.zh: 让我们假设他们是个好射手，投篮命中率为50%。

sentences.en: That 50% probability is going to produce a lot more clumping in the baskets than people expect.
sentences.zh: 这个50%的概率会比人们预期的产生更多的进球聚集。

sentences.en: People expect a coin flip, a 50% probability,
sentences.zh: 人们期望抛硬币这种50%概率的事件，

sentences.en: to alternate a lot more than it actually does.
sentences.zh: 其交替出现的频率要比实际发生的高得多。

sentences.en: And so when you see randomness out in the world,
sentences.zh: 所以当你看到世界上的随机性时，

sentences.en: it actually looks more ordered to you than it really is.
sentences.zh: 它在你看来实际上比真正的随机更有秩序。

sentences.en: Epley described a party trick that demonstrates this phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 埃普利描述了一个展示这种现象的派对把戏。

sentences.en: You can do this too.
sentences.zh: 你也可以这样做。

sentences.en: Give everyone in the party a note card
sentences.zh: 给派对上的每个人一张便条卡，

sentences.en: and have them write down what they think 30 coin flips would look like.
sentences.zh: 让他们写下他们认为30次抛硬币会是什么样子。

sentences.en: H if they think it'll be heads,
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为是正面就写H，

sentences.en: T if they think it'll be tails.
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为是反面就写T。

sentences.en: You then, as master magician, leave the room
sentences.zh: 然后，作为魔术大师的你离开房间，

sentences.en: and you have one person come up and actually flip a coin 30 times.
sentences.zh: 让一个人上来真正抛30次硬币。

sentences.en: That person writes down the actual sequence of coin flips on a note card
sentences.zh: 那个人把真实的抛硬币序列写在一张便条卡上，

sentences.en: and then collects all the note cards, the real and the imagined sequences,
sentences.zh: 然后收集所有的便条卡——真实的和想象的序列，

sentences.en: and puts them together.
sentences.zh: 把它们放在一起。

sentences.en: You, the magician, then come back into the room
sentences.zh: 身为魔术师的你随后回到房间，

sentences.en: and identify the card that was the real coin flip.
sentences.zh: 找出那张真正抛硬币的卡片。

sentences.en: And the way you do this is you look for the card that has the longest runs
sentences.zh: 你这样做的办法是寻找拥有最长连续相同结果的卡片，

sentences.en: because people's imagination doesn't presume
sentences.zh: 因为人们的想象并不认为

sentences.en: that a 50-50 probability will produce very long runs.
sentences.zh: 50对50的概率会产生很长的连续结果。

sentences.en: And so people's imagined coin flips will alternate more than the real coin flip will.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们想象的抛硬币结果交替的频率会比真实的抛硬币更高。

sentences.en: And that's how you can identify the real one from the fake ones.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如何从假卡片中识别出真卡片的方法。

sentences.en: And I think that illusion that we have that randomness alternates
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所拥有的那种随机性会交替出现

sentences.en: or is more chancy than it actually is,
sentences.zh: 或者比实际情况更具偶然性的错觉，

sentences.en: that there's less clumping,
sentences.zh: 那种认为结果聚集较少的想法，

sentences.en: is also the thing that gives rise to these other phenomena
sentences.zh: 也是滋生其他现象的原因，

sentences.en: where we see randomness in the world
sentences.zh: 在这些现象中，我们在世事中看到随机性，

sentences.en: and we see more predictability or intentionality than actually exists in it.
sentences.zh: 却看到了比其中实际存在的更多的可预测性或意图性。

sentences.en: When we asked our listeners to share coincidences with us,
sentences.zh: 当我们请听众与我们分享巧合时，

sentences.en: many of them wrote in with really interesting examples of things that happened to them.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人写信分享了发生在他身上的非常有趣的例子。

sentences.en: One thing that I was struck by is the sense that sometimes
sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的一点是，有时你会觉得

sentences.en: a coincidence seems more meaningful to you than it does to someone else.
sentences.zh: 一个巧合对你来说比对别人更有意义。

sentences.en: So, for example, when I'm reading a book and I come by an unusual word
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，当我正在读一本书，偶然看到一个不寻常的词，

sentences.en: and then someone in the room mentions that same word,
sentences.zh: 然后房间里有人提到了这个词，

sentences.en: to me it feels like it's a sign of something.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这感觉像是某种预兆。

sentences.en: But if I were to tell you, I say,
sentences.zh: 但如果我把这事告诉你，我说：

sentences.en: Nick, you know, this happened to me yesterday,
sentences.zh: 尼克，你知道吗，昨天发生了这种事，

sentences.en: you'd say, yeah, sure, that's going to happen once every month or so.
sentences.zh: 你会说，哦得了吧，这大概每隔一个月左右就会发生一次。

sentences.en: It's exactly what you would expect if you believe the laws of probability.
sentences.zh: 如果你相信概率定律，这正是你会预料到的。

sentences.en: Why do you think it is that coincidences are more meaningful to us than to other people?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么巧合对我们而言比对其他人更有意义？

sentences.en: That's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I actually don't know that I've seen any research that demonstrates that phenomena,
sentences.zh: 其实我不知道我是否见过任何研究来证明这种现象，

sentences.en: but that strikes me as a very compelling hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这是一个非常引人注目的假设。

sentences.en: I think that's probably likely to be right.
sentences.zh: 我想这很可能是对的。

sentences.en: And I think the reason why coincidences seem very meaningful in the first place
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，巧合之所以一开始看起来很有意义，

sentences.en: is that you're trying to explain them.
sentences.zh: 是因为你正试图解释它们。

sentences.en: You and I both thought of the word propeller at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你和我同时想到了“螺旋桨”这个词。

sentences.en: How on earth could that be that Shankar was thinking about propeller at the same time that I was?
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔怎么会跟我同时想到“螺旋桨”呢？这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And so you're trying to explain that.
sentences.zh: 所以你正试图解释这一点。

sentences.en: You're focusing on that event that just happened to you.
sentences.zh: 你专注于刚刚发生在自己身上的那个事件。

sentences.en: It has personal relevance to you.
sentences.zh: 它与你有着个人的相关性。

sentences.en: That makes it impactful.
sentences.zh: 这让它具有冲击力。

sentences.en: But it also makes you somewhat myopic.
sentences.zh: 但这也让你变得有些目光短浅。

sentences.en: And what we don't think about are all of the other things
sentences.zh: 而我们没有去想的是，房间里的任何一个人

sentences.en: that any of us in the room could have thought about at the same time
sentences.zh: 在同一时间还可能想到过的所有其他事情，

sentences.en: that might also have seemed amazing to us.
sentences.zh: 那些事情对我们来说也可能显得很神奇。

sentences.en: We're trying to explain this one thing because it's so meaningful to us.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图解释这一件特定的事情，因为它对我们太有意义了。

sentences.en: It just happened to us.
sentences.zh: 它刚刚发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: Other people are less likely to be that myopic, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，其他人没那么容易变得如此目光短浅。

sentences.en: And so they would be likely to think about other things that could have happened to you,
sentences.zh: 所以他们很可能会去想其他可能发生在你身上的事情，

sentences.en: which would make it seem less amazing to them.
sentences.zh: 这会让他们觉得这没那么神奇。

sentences.en: We, of course, experienced this ourselves here at the show
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在节目里也亲自经历过这种情况，

sentences.en: when two listeners called in with eerily similar coincidence stories.
sentences.zh: 当时两位听众打进电话，讲述了极其相似的巧合故事。

sentences.en: I described these two stories to Nick about women who ran into people
sentences.zh: 我向尼克描述了这两个故事，关于两个女性遇到了这样的人：

sentences.en: who turned out to live in the very same house where the women's parents had grown up.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然住在这些女性的父母小时候长大的同一所房子里。

sentences.en: So these are not just two coincidences.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是两个巧合。

sentences.en: These are two coincidences that both happened to us at Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 这是两个巧合，而且都发生在我们《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）节目身上，

sentences.en: which seems truly extraordinary, Nick.
sentences.zh: 尼克，这看起来真的太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: How could that possibly be that you get these two that are exactly the same?
sentences.zh: 怎么可能会遇到这两个一模一样的故事呢？

sentences.en: It's magic is what it is, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 这就是魔法，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: You're magical.
sentences.zh: 你很有魔法。

sentences.en: That's really just all I wanted to hear you say, Nick.
sentences.zh: 尼克，这其实就是我想听你说的全部。

sentences.en: It's been 20 minutes to get that out of you.
sentences.zh: 花了20分钟才让你说出这句话。

sentences.en: Eventually, we have to give in to the laws of probability.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们不得不向概率定律妥协。

sentences.en: There's nothing that can explain that, right?
sentences.zh: 没有什么能解释这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Nick, I want to thank you for talking with us today.
sentences.zh: 尼克，我想谢谢你今天跟我们交谈。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.zh: 尼克·埃普利（Nick Epley），他是《思维智慧：》，

sentences.en: How We Understand What Others Think, Believe, Feel, and Want.
sentences.zh: 《我们如何理解别人的想法、信念、感受和愿望》（MindWise: How We Understand What Others Think, Believe, Feel, and Want）一书的作者。

sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》由Hidden Brain Media制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的制作团队包括布里奇特·麦卡锡（Bridget McCarthy）、瑞安·卡茨（Ryan Katz）、克里斯滕·王（Kristen Wong）、

sentences.zh: 劳拉·奎雷尔（Laura Querell）、奥特姆·巴恩斯（Autumn Barnes）以及安德鲁·查德威克（Andrew Chadwick）。

sentences.zh: 我们的执行制作人是塔拉·博伊尔（Tara Boyle）。

sentences.zh: 我是《隐藏的大脑》的执行主编。

sentences.zh: 当这期节目在2016年首次发布时，

sentences.zh: 那是我们第一次表彰一位无名英雄。

sentences.en: In the years since then, this moment at the end of our show
sentences.zh: 从那以后的几年里，我们节目结束时的这一时刻

sentences.zh: 已成为我们《隐秘大脑》节目中不可或缺的重要部分。

sentences.en: Our very first unsung hero was Mathilde Piard,
sentences.zh: 我们的第一位无名英雄是马蒂尔德·皮阿尔，

sentences.en: a senior project manager at NPR.
sentences.zh: 她是美国国家公共广播电台的高级项目经理。

sentences.en: She knew everything about everything,
sentences.zh: 她无所不知，

sentences.en: and as Hidden Brain launched into the world,
sentences.zh: 随着《隐秘大脑》走向世界，

sentences.en: she played an important role in getting it started.
sentences.zh: 她在节目的创立过程中发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: She was always generous with her time
sentences.zh: 她总是毫不吝啬地付出时间，

sentences.en: and generous with her knowledge.
sentences.zh: 也总是慷慨地分享她的知识。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mathilde.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，马蒂尔德。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢本期节目，请考虑支持我们的工作。

sentences.zh: 你可以访问 support.hiddenbrain.org 来支持我们

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 我们下周见。
